London, 27<sup>th</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Eastern Platinum Limited’s** President and CEO Ian Rozier announced that production from the Crocodile River Mine for the fourth quarter ended December 31, 2008 reached 29,015 ounces. _Source:  Eastern Platinum_ 

**Platinum Australia Limited** announced that following the successful ore commissioning of the crushing and milling sections of the Processing Plant at the Smokey Hills Platinum Mine in South Africa, the first flotation concentrates were produced on Friday 23rd January.   It is now anticipated that the first shipment of concentrates to the Impala Platinum Smelter will occur within the next week to ten days. _Source:  Trading Markets/Platinum Australia_ 

**Blackthorn Resources** has been granted its new order prospecting rights, over the Mokopane nickel/ platinum project, in South Africa’s Limpopo province.  The renewal of the prospecting right was valid until April 2011, and would have to be lodged with the Mineral and Petroleum Titles office within 30 days, to register the title.  “This is another great opportunity for the company to progress and develop one of its assets…Blackthorn Resources is currently looking at strategic options to add value to this project,” said company MD Scott Lowe. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Anglo Platinum** reported that development work at its Paardekraal Two shaft had been halted after one of its workers died over the weekend.  The Department of Minerals and Energy closed the shaft soon thereafter, to remain closed while the company conducted an investigation.   Production would not be affected, as the shaft was still in the development phase.  The Paardekraal Two shaft would be completed in two phases, with vertical depths of between 1 100 m and 1 200 m. The project was expected to be complete by November 2014. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Anglo Platinum** was yesterday lowered to underweight from neutral by JPMorgan Chase as a slump in prices left the company “haemorrhaging cash”. _Source:  Business Report_ 

**President Barack Obama** is set to allow California to regulate greenhouse-gas emissions for autos, reversing a Bush administration ruling.  More than a dozen other U.S. states may then adopt the same standards, which are opposed by automakers.  General Motors, Ford , Chrysler LLC and companies represented by the Alliance of Automobile Manufacturers trade group sued to block California’s rules, arguing that developing vehicles that comply would cost billions of dollars. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Honda** is cutting production in North America and Japan by another 50,000 vehicles to match rapidly shrinking demand.  The move slashes projected North American output to 1.264 million units for the fiscal year ending March 31, 12.0 % lower than the previous year and 13.9 % below Honda’s initial forecast of 1.468 million vehicles this year.  In Japan, the carmaker is cutting output by 21,000 units. That will bring domestic

production to 1.147 million units this fiscal year.  The new total is down 12% from a year ago and down 12.4 % from Honda’s original target of making 1.31 million vehicles at home. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**General Motors** will cut about 2,000 jobs at two plants and plans periodic shutdowns at about half of its 16 U.S. factories as consumers continue to shun new vehicles. _Source:  Automotive News_
